query: Consider the following context: High-temperature self-lubricating materials with stable tribological performance across a wide temperature range are essential for advanced mechanical systems under extreme conditions. However, balancing mechanical strength and lubrication efficiency remains a key challenge. In that context, which material can be used for high-performance wide-temperature self-lubricating materials, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Using powder metallurgy to create a composite material of titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-4V) with 10% graphite and 5% molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) will result in a high-performance wide-temperature self-lubricating material with stable tribological performance across a temperature range of 20°C to 500°C.
generation.material_initial_state: Ti-6Al-4V alloy powder with 10% graphite and 5% MoS2
generation.intervention: Powder metallurgy processing with hot isostatic pressing (HIP) at 900°C and 100 MPa for 2 hours
generation.conditions: Temperature range: 20°C to 500°C, sliding speed: 0.1 m/s, normal load: 100 N
generation.structural_mediator: Homogeneous distribution of graphite and MoS2 solid lubricants in the Ti-6Al-4V alloy matrix
generation.mechanism: Graphite and MoS2 solid lubricants reduce friction and wear by forming a transfer film on the counterface, while the Ti-6Al-4V alloy matrix provides mechanical strength and stability
generation.predicted_outcome: Coefficient of friction (COF) reduction of 30% and wear rate reduction of 50% compared to the baseline material (Ti-6Al-4V alloy without solid lubricants)
generation.uncertainty: The actual performance of the composite material may vary depending on the processing conditions, solid lubricant distribution, and testing parameters

falsification_experiment.design: Tribological testing using a pin-on-disk tribometer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the COF reduction is less than 20% or the wear rate reduction is less than 30% compared to the baseline material, the hypothesis is falsified

frame.limitation: balancing mechanical strength and lubrication efficiency
